So whatever the producer, the cinemaist [sic], et cetera, did in this film, I have no concern and no responsibility in it. I am totally disconnected from this cinematic event.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Is this character wearing glasses, is that Calvez in the movie?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is Benoit Magimel, yes, a French actor.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. And the wounded man, is he pointing with his finger at a photo of General Tolimir?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you can see it in this extract of a fiction movie, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ruez. Could you tell us what comes to mind when you see this photo from this movie, this still?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, the orientations taken by those who did this film are not of my concern because I didn't give them a hand to do this film.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: So you cannot tell us what this brings to mind, or can you? What does this photo remind you of?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection. Time is of the essence, and vague questions regarding movies and unreal worlds don't take us anywhere, and I would object to this kind of question. The fact that there is a real photograph of Tolimir, no problem. But your impressions of a movie, this isn't a place for -- you know, time for movie critiques, especially when this witness has nothing to do with this film.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, you several times mentioned that there are time restraints. You should deal with the real facts and look at the time. Please -- you have indicated that you will use several documents, but this is perhaps not the best way to deal with evidence. Please go ahead. Please don't -- no discussion now. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Could we now please see the last part of the movie, as the witness said that this character is actually depicting him? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, this is not correct. It is not the witness; it is a movie with actors. And you received the comment of this witness, Mr. Ruez, on that. If you have a question, put it to him, but think of the time.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I did put the question, Is this actor that we see now before us with glasses, is that Calvez? And he said that it was. And now I would just like to see -- for us to see the next photo. Could we please play this video-clip from one minute thirty-three -- 1.33:39 to 1:35:40. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, what is the purpose of showing us a video of a movie, what is the purpose of that? Is that kind of evidence?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I wanted to show here that this witness participated in the preparations for this movie because he did confirm that this actor -- this character is probably him, the character that we can now see on our screens with the glasses. And if we could now just see the photos as I requested, the stills that I requested, and we will then end up with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Let's see this seven seconds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Not to waste time, Mr. Tolimir, you should perhaps now stop that and put questions to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, what could you see now here in these final clips of this movie? Could you tell us?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: As we all did, scenes from the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Were these actual facts and actual snap-shots or video stills of an actual courtroom here?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: These picture even bear on them the logo of the ICTY, so I'm quite sure, indeed, they are extracts from the courtroom trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it common practice to use actual footage from a courtroom with real accused in propaganda-purpose movies of this type?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, you should be aware of the fact that all trials are recorded in the internet, also this trial here in this courtroom, and is available for the whole public around the world. Everybody can use it. That has been done several times. Also, this trial today is recorded in the internet.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President, but that footage is not used for propaganda. Could we now just see a video-clip which will explain why I have shown this, and I would appreciate it if we could see the still at two minutes three seconds. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Would you please tell us the number of this document?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is just the same movie, the same video-clip, a continuation of it. 1D76. Thank you. We have some technical problems, so I'll move on to the next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: From what you know, when was it, in July, that Mladic met Calves for the first time, and was this at the Fontana Hotel on the 11th of July that we saw in this movie a few moments ago?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It might be a problem of interpretation or you mentioned the wrong name. I think you were not referring to Mr. Calves, but to Mr. Karremans. Are you?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct. It's possible that I misspoke. I meant Karremans. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I remember, there were two meetings, one -- one which is the one that you have shown, and there was one -- a second one a bit later, when Colonel Karremans managed to find Nesib Mandzic, and he returned to Hotel Fontana for a meeting with General Mladic and his aides together with Nesib Mandzic. This is where he explained him that, We had to surrender, adding a choice, You have the choice to survive or disappear. So that, I think, was the second meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Tell me, please, was this the first meeting we saw in the video-clip showing General Mladic and General Karremans? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think it was the first one.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we now just see an excerpt from the video-clip that we prepared. The entire video-clip is two hours and twenty-two minutes' long, but we will just show the two hours -- just the twenty-five seconds from two hours twenty-nine minutes forty-nine seconds, the so-called Srebrenica video-clip. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We have some technical problems. Could we please see the film -- a video-clip from "Resolution 819."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, you've seen this excerpt from this video-clip, and earlier you saw the video-clip from Fontana Hotel that we couldn't show for technical problems. Now, my question is this: The way General Mladic is depicted in this video-clip, is that something that is normally how he's depicted in the Western media?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not a media critic. Please ask me questions related to the investigation, not to this movie. I repeat, my participation in this has been extremely limited, since I accepted to read back the scenario just in order to extract from it things that could be completely irrelevant, and I decided not to retrieve anything because I didn't want to take any part of any kind of responsibility with this scenario. This is it, so I have no -- no control and no vision about this film. I'm not part of it, though, indeed, the main character is supposed to be me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ruez. Is the scene that we saw just a moment ago, where General Mladic was on the tank, was that a fictitious scene or was it actually realistic or real?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The thing that we at the OTP take responsibility for is the two-hour and something video that we, indeed, name "The Srebrenica Video," and in which, indeed, you can see the behaviour of General Mladic. So to match his behaviour with this fiction, anyone can do it. You don't need my assessment on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: I only ask whether this was an actual situation that existed, that happened in Srebrenica, or not. Just yes or no. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: A fiction is never a reflection of a reality. The reality of the statements made by General Mladic and who exist on video have been presented by the Prosecution, and you have seen these videos.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ruez. You didn't want to answer my question. May we now have two video footages played from the Fontana Hotel. These are authentic videos. But while that is being prepared, I would like to ask you something about the position of the OTP and Prosecution in all the Srebrenica -- in the Srebrenica affair, and it is page 450. You will see that the window was opened so that everybody inside could hear the screams of a pig being slaughtered. Can we show that, please. Mr. Ruez, let me ask you this: The fact that the pig was being slaughtered during the meeting with Karremans, did you attach any symbolic importance to that? That's my question to you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: In any case, it had a very symbolic importance for the person who was present there, who is Nesib Mandzic. He's the one who reported the importance he attached to this, in itself, insignificant event, but in these circumstances had, for him, a big significance.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we be shown 1D62 now, please. It's a document from the Drina Corps Command, entitled "Permission for the Slaughter of Animals," and I'd like to quote from that. But may we have the document up on our screens first, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I would request that the general play the video, as he said he would, because that is what gives the context to the question and these other documents. I don't know why he's not, but he said he was, and that was the context to the question. I think he should follow through with it so the Court understands what this is about.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We'll play the footage when we hear the witness's answer. Thank you. 1D62 is the next document I'd like displayed, please. It's from the Drina Corps Command, "Permission for Slaughter and Issue of Livestock." And in point 2, it says, and I quote: "Permission is granted for the slaughter and delivery for the needs of the UN soldiers billeted in the hotel in Bratunac of the following: A hog up to 80 kilograms. The hog shall be delivered to the hotel in Bratunac on orders from the Command of the Drina Corps."

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Ruez, this is a document dated the 10th of July, when the Fontana Hotel meeting was taking place. Was it on the 11th of July, in the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: 11, not the 10. I mean, the document might indicate the 10, but the meeting was the 11.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Ruez. Now may we show part of the footage where the slaughter of the hog is heard, and then what General Mladic says, and then what General Mladic says at the third Fontana Hotel meeting. Thank you. May that be played, please, from the first minute to one minute forty-five seconds. Can we play that excerpt, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, what we've just seen, the hand-shaking and the joint meeting, can that be considered as instilling fear and exerting pressure on UNPROFOR in any way?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the third meeting, the one at 12, in the morning, where the three representatives of the, in bracket, Muslim population are at Fontana.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, that was not the portion of the video you indicated to show when we hear the -- we hear the noise of the slaughtered pig.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's right. We'll try again. The technical booth will try and find it and play it for us. That was the wrong excerpt. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, you've just seen this excerpt, part of the footage, where the slaughter of the pig is shown for propaganda purposes, and you saw the participants in the meeting between Mladic and the rest. Now, tell me, in reality, was this pressure exerted or was it relaxation?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please pause a moment. I was just told that the person is a protected witness. If that is correct, it should be redacted, the name. Perhaps you can help us, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Could we go into private session briefly, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, please carry on. You may continue. We have still five minutes left until the second break.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: I'm now going to quote a statement made by Mr. Mirsad Tokaca, presented at the conference. It's a document that we referred to yesterday about Srebrenica, and what was found, and what the director of the centre came up with. He told journalists the following: "During our investigation and project --" May we have 1D114 called up, please. I've just been advised that we need it on our screens so that you can all follow. We'll wait for a moment until it does come up on our screens. 1D114, please. Do you see this document? The title is "Tokaca," and he says: "We found 500 people from Srebrenica who are alive and who are listed as missing." And now I'm going to quote from that statement of his. It says: "During our investigation and project, we found about 500 living people from Srebrenica. We also have information that a little more than 7.000 people were killed in the area, but they were not all from Srebrenica. There are people from various other towns; Vlasenica, Zvornik, Bratunac, Visegrad, and so on. Seventy persons were buried in the Memorial Centre, Potocari, which did not lose their lives in Srebrenica, said Tokaca to journalists in Banja Luka."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: For the record, you quoted from the last paragraph of that page; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is correct, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: What is your question for the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: My question is this: During the investigation, did you receive information about the fact that not all those people listed as missing were in Srebrenica in July 1995? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I think Mr. Tokaca means when he says all the people were not from Srebrenica is, indeed, the fact that when this enclave spontaneously created itself in 1992, very little of the people who were there were from Srebrenica. Indeed, those who scrambled in that place were those who were the victims of the ethnic cleansing of -- at the north of Zvornik and, at the west, Vlasenica. So these people were coming from the entire big area, and this is also the reason why, when they had to flee, the reference point was this power line, because most of these people didn't know at all this area.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Ruez.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Judge Nyambe has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: The question that was asked was: "During the investigation, did you receive information about the fact that not all those people listed as missing were in Srebrenica in 1995?"

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, since on the ICRC list all those who -- there is a column that says from where these people are missing from, so the entire number, according to ICRC, was missing from Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: So your simple answer is you did not receive that information during your investigations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to thank Judge Nyambe for asking that question. I was about to do that, and the witness has now clarified the position.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Now, did you check the list of the International Red Cross on missing persons and the list of those who were buried at Potocari? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is one specific expert on this question who was tasked to look into that matter in preparation of the trial of General Krstic. I believe his full report is accessible from the record of that trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you or did you not compare the list of the ICRC -- the missing persons list of the ICRC with those who were buried in Potocari? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not specifically with those buried in Potocari. There are very, very few people who were buried in Potocari. All the main crime scenes, as I showed in my direct, they were not in Potocari. Again, you should -- I can only refer you to the report of this demographer who was the expert for these questions during the trial of General Krstic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir and all others in the courtroom, we must have the second break now. You should prepare the remainder of your cross-examination very carefully for only half an hour. Thank you. We adjourn and resume at 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I'd like to tender 1D111 and 1D14 [as interpreted], the one we've just shown, and 1D62. 1D111, 1D114, and 1D62. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think the parts he played -- well, I have no objection to the Hotel Fontana, though we have the whole thing in already. If it's helpful for the record to have that blip, that's no problem. The Tokaca newspaper article, I would not object to, so long as I can provide you with the retraction by that organisation that say they were taken out of context by the Serb Crna News Agency, which I'm sure the general is fully aware of. And we have a 65 ter number for that now, 6237. Though given Mr. Ruez's answer to the general's question, there's no point in me showing the retraction to Mr. Ruez, given that Mr. Ruez didn't know about the first article. But there's just a short retraction of it to put it in context. Though, of course, you will be hearing, I'm sorry, from experts on the issue of the missing, and the lists, and all this material will be thrown out. But I just -- a one-sided article sitting there like that, out of context, that the witness didn't know anything about, I didn't want -- I only wanted if you could see the other half of it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you, and the Chamber will consider that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, we have a problem because you were not tendering these documents at the proper time when you showed this document. Now it's a little bit later. You should be aware of the proper proceedings. We will receive the portion of the video from the Hotel Fontana meeting we have seen today, because that was already shown at length at the beginning of the trial, but not tendered yet by the Prosecution. We will receive today only this portion. We start with that. That is, I think -- which number, if the Court Officer will help us?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think that is the number 1D111. If that is correct, that will be received. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And 1D62, the Drina Corps document about the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Just we would like to have this number, exhibit number, on the record. One moment.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 1D111 will be Exhibit D36, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. And then the other document related to the slaughter and delivery of the hog, 1D62, we have no objection to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I'm not sure if we saw the English translation of that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No, we probably didn't, so I -- we should, of course, follow the procedure then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I got the information that there is an English translation. Therefore, we will receive it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 1D62 will be Exhibit D38, Your Honour -- D37, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. And the third one is the excerpt from the internet, from a web site, with a certain Mr. Tokaca. That will be marked for identification, since there is no English translation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be D38, marked for identification, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, please carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. We were discussing the document before the break, and there was just one sentence that I didn't manage to quote, which is vital for this Trial Chamber. It's important that you hear the sentence when you come to decide on the document. Tokaca says, and I quote, at the end: "The greatest problem was in --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, we just marked this document for identification. There will be a translation, and that is part of the evidence. It is -- we have everything what we need. Please bear in mind you have 20 minutes left. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I just wanted to read out one sentence so that I can ask my question. But you're not going to allowed me to do that. Never mind. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, was there a problem with the monopoly of information, as it's called, when it comes to information that you were able to glean about Srebrenica? And Mr. Tokaca uses the term here "monopoly of information." Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know nothing about the investigation Mr. Tokaca conducted. I don't know what means he had to conduct it. I don't know the conclusions that he drafted. Again, these things were done totally independently by him. If he refers to a monopoly of information that we might have had at that time, I don't know. I don't believe so. Yes, we had more means, for sure, both technically and ability to move in Republika Srpska, because we had the armed forces to protect us. But I believe this is maybe what he means by "monopoly of information."

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. As I don't have more time, I'd like to look at 1D77 next, please. While we're waiting for the document to be called up, 1D77, let me explain what it's about to the witness. It's an interview which a French intelligence officer, Bunel, gave to Zoran Petrovic in 2004, and it was published in a weekly called "Evropa." It was in the disclosure package and disclosed by the Prosecution. Here we have it on our screens. It says: "But as far as Srebrenica is concerned, I remember, and I said this and wrote it, that in the spring of 1996, we saw Muslim men of good health coming out of the woods in order to report to the American division in Tuzla. There was several hundred of them, and they said that they had left Srebrenica after the fall of the town. Therefore, they were not massacred, but the Americans gathered them together and took them out of the region in an unknown direction. Some of them went on to the United States. We were not able to interview them in order to learn what had actually happened." Now, tell me this: Did you have this piece of information at the time when you were the principal investigator? Yes or no, please, because I haven't got much time.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. And there were no American forces in Tuzla at that time, so I'm astonished about such a statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. The American forces were in the base all the time in the environs of Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, negative. There was a Swedish base, and the air base become Eagle Base at the end of 1995 and mainly during the year 1996.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We'll leave it up to the Trial Chamber to check and see who is right and who is wrong, and I'll go on to my next question since my time is expiring. May we have 1D114 called up again, please, the document we were looking at earlier on. No, that's a mistake. Sorry, we've already seen that. We don't need it again. I do apologise. My next question is this, Mr. Ruez -- 65 ter 142 is the next document I would like us to look at and to be called up on our screens, please, on e-court. While we're waiting for that, I'll tell you what it's about. Mr. Ruez, in this document, we see that it is the Prosecutor versus Rasim Delic, and there the Prosecution advocated and proposed to the Trial Chamber the following, and I'm going to read an excerpt from the judgement, a quotation from the judgement. I gave the wrong number, I've just been told. It's 1D101. 1D101, please. May we have page 2 displayed, please. I'll read out what it says: "The Prosecution submits that the Trial Chamber should --" Well, paragraph 32 or the footnote of paragraph 32, it is part of the judgement and suggestions made by the Prosecution as follows: "The Trial Chamber should exercise extreme caution when considering the testimony of witnesses who are former members of the BH Army. It contends that their versions of the events might represent a form of historical revisionism, as these witnesses would have a motive to deny anything that might call into question the sincerity of the goal of maintaining a secular multi-ethnic Bosnia." End of quotation from the Prosecution's final trial brief.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Ruez, when you interviewed people -- or, rather, when you gave interviews and assessed testimony, did you exercise extreme caution with respect to the Muslims' goal of presenting themselves as being victims; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ruez -- well, first of all, I'd like to tender document 1D142 into evidence, please, a 65 ter document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You want to tender the whole document or just part of the judgement?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just the portion that I quoted. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: He made reference to the Prosecution trial brief and now the judgement. I'm not sure what he's asking for, but neither are appropriate to be part of this trial record. I think it's a fair use of a statement or a judgement to question the witness on, but I don't think it's helpful to the Court to have someone else's judgement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Do you have any comments to the objection of Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. The witness's answer was, Yes, to my question, and that's why I wanted this to be admitted into evidence, because the witness said, Yes, with no further comment. Thank you. I didn't want to expose him to any other situation. All I asked was for a yes-or-no answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, this judgement is on the record and on the JDB and everywhere available for everybody. You have quoted a portion of this judgement, and the witness stated, Yes. That's all. Is it really necessary to receive this part?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I won't insist because I have no more time. I don't want to waste my time. You can decide in due course, and I will accept any ruling and decision you make. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received. That means paragraph 32 and the front page of this judgement.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 65 ter 1D101 will be Exhibit D39, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: In fact, the first page and paragraph 32. Carry on, please, Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Ruez -- may we have 1D59 called up, please, page 6 of that document. Thank you. And I'll tell you what it's about while we're waiting for it to appear. It's your statement given to "The Monitor," and on page 6 in Serbian, in paragraph 2, it says the following -- it's a statement that you gave to the parliamentary -- at the parliamentary hearing. Paragraph 2 of page 6, just one sentence, and please give me a yes-or-no answer: "I have to stress one more important point. I heard that all that -- that members of the paramilitaries were involved in all that. However, Arkan did not take part in that operation. All the executions were carried out by the regular units of the Drina Corps or special units attached to the Main Staff of the army." Thank you. Have I correctly quoted your words before the parliamentary hearing in France?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, would you -- would you have the -- would you dare to say this publicly so that we can see that nobody from Serbia took part in the executions in Srebrenica and, in that way, to put a stop to the Satanisation of the Serbs? Do you dare -- can you do that without permission from your Parliament and this Tribunal? Can you repeat what you stated to the Parliamentary Commission? I think that that would be important for reconciliation. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I gave that statement, if I recall well, in 2001. Unfortunately, since then, as you know, came out the video of this paramilitary group named the Skorpions, who can be seen in lifetime executing six youngsters originated from Srebrenica. So, unfortunately, I cannot please you by saying that no one from the other side of the river participated.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ruez. Do you know that this group, Skorpions, does not belong to Serbia, but to the former Republic of Srpska Krajina and, in particular, that portion of it which belonged to Vukovar as a centre?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't. But, in addition, I'm very pleased that, indeed, these people were put on trial in Serbia and severely condemned by Serb justice.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. But at the time, they weren't citizens of Serbia. They were citizens of Republika Srpska Krajina. Now, for this Tribunal and this Trial Chamber, can you confirm that during your investigations you saw that neither Arkan nor any paramilitaries from Serbia had been involved? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Ruez. I would like to ask this Trial Chamber to admit this document, 1D -- ah, I've been told that it's already an exhibit, already in evidence, so thank you, that 1D59 is already in evidence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, I am told that it is not an exhibit yet. If you have different information --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If it isn't, then I would like to tender it because it's important. The witness has stated what he said on the basis of the results of his investigations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit D40, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, we do not object to that exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You have a few minutes left. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, you -- in your statements here, and I don't have enough time to go into them all and to quote them all in the various documents, but, anyway, on several occasions you mentioned General Tolimir, whereas we haven't been able to see the footage of that because of the technical problems. Can you tell this Trial Chamber whether you -- in the documents, while you were working in Srebrenica, did you find General Tolimir, and in talking -- in talking to the witnesses that you interviewed, was General Tolimir mentioned?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That will be more a question for the military analyst of the situation, but you are right. With those who I interviewed, both on the victim side and on the Bosnian Serb Army side, your name didn't pop up during these interviews.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Ruez. Mr. President, I would like to thank you. I have adhered to my time-limit. My time is up, I see, and I thank you. Allow me to thank Mr. Ruez, too, for his very proper conduct, and I hope he won't be angry with me for showing part of the film which denies that I was involved and -- it refutes that I was involved, and the screenwriter shows this. I would like to thank the Trial Chamber. I would like to thank the interpreters and apologise for the problems I've caused them. I wish you all a very happy weekend, and God bless you all. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, thank you for your nice comments for the witness. On the other hand, we are not at the beginning of the weekend, regrettably. Mr. McCloskey, do you have re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, you were questioned at length about the investigation and the evidence that you recalled related to the number of people and people at the soccer pitch in Nova Kasaba. I'm referring, in particular, to 1575, lines 3 through 10, at some point where you spoke of information that you had reviewed that may not be in the record, that may not be part of the witnesses on that subject. You also spoke briefly about reviewing war crimes commission statements and MUP statements early on in the investigation, so I'm going to take you way back and see if you can recall some of this, and I'll start with what we've marked as number 6234. That's a 65 ter number, and it should come up on your screen. And this is, as you'll see, a summary of a war crimes commission statement, and I can tell you I've learned that it was a summary that was made on the 11th of November, 1996, by your team. This is -- the front page that we're seeing is the Bosnian version, which we can see up in the English it actually says "State Commission for Gathering Facts," and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, I'm not sure if the accused dealt with this document during cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No, he didn't. He repeatedly pressed the witness on information he had about information based on people at the soccer field, and that's when Mr. Ruez said, I reviewed other documents that may not be part of the record. And what I'm attempting to do is see if Mr. Ruez recalls reviewing other documents so that you understand that that was -- whether or not that happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can you show us on the screen so then we can check it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. Unfortunately, the document I wanted to show him has -- is not immediately available. So if I could put it on the ELMO, because it's only in English. You know, Mr. President, let's just go on. I will skip that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. But if we're going to read this, could I also have the Serbian version before me, because I don't know what this is about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, Mr. McCloskey just indicated that he will skip that document and not dwell on that. It should be removed from the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: On the same topic, Mr. Ruez, do you recall reviewing some of the DutchBat statements that were made during your time regarding what some DutchBat officers saw as they went up and down that road on those dates?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember reviewing all the statements that were taken by others from DutchBat members.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to 65 ter 6231, and there is an original Dutch version of that. And we want the English version up on the screen at the moment. All right. And if we could blow that up a little bit, we'll note that the date of the interview was 24 October 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Were you the team leader at that time?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And the interview was --

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry. What is the date?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: 24 October 1995. You'll see it down in the left-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Officially, I was not the team leader, because there was no team dedicated to that until the end of 1996. But --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I'm very sorry. I have to interrupt you. I'm not sure if this is a proper and acceptable document during re-examination. I see there was an interview, Irma Oosterman. We haven't seen this before, and the witness didn't give evidence about this topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, he was -- the foundation -- the reason I'm bringing this forward is that Mr. Ruez was challenged repeatedly about his investigation, and the thoroughness of investigation, and what he learned throughout the investigation on this particular topic of the number of people that are at the field at Nova Kasaba. And so when Mr. Tolimir brings up that issue and challenges Mr. Ruez on his investigation and the evidence that he collected, I think it's appropriate for me to go back and see if Mr. Ruez can recollect whether this is part of the evidence that he relies on when he testifies to you that there are so many people on the football field. And I can also tell you Mr. Egbers is on the witness list, and so this will be someone that will be fully able to be cross-examined, I do believe. So it's not something I'm trying to get in without, of course, cross-examination. But when the challenge is on the investigation and his information that he has, that door is opened, and I should be allowed to see if Mr. Ruez remembers this and whether he may have relied upon it, when you're judging his credibility and the attack that was a strong attack on his credibility related to the witnesses that put information about Nova Kasaba.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: He told us he was not the team leader at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: He told us he was not the formal team leader because that did not happen, formally, until later. But if we ask him what he was doing, which I was going to follow up on, you know, you will hear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Taking into account your explanation, why you are putting this document to the witness, the Chamber is satisfied with your course of re-examination. If there is any reason, then we should leave the possibility for the accused to raise another question to that topic. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, can you explain to us -- you said you weren't formally the team leader in October 24th. What were you then?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: In fact, at that time I was a member of the investigation team dealing with the investigation on the siege of Sarajevo. But after I started working on this investigation and during the summer 1995, I was later, in fact, the only person who was full-time working on this topic. The other colleagues could provide me some assistance from time to time mainly when going on mission, but as soon as the mission was over they were returning to their other activities. So, in fact, I was the only person full-time in charge of the case, so I was de facto the team leader for this -- the investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So would you have been team leader when you reviewed this document?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: In fact, I took on myself to collect absolutely all the statements that we had collected during the month -- end of July and August, plus later also those from the interview process of the members of DutchBat, and this in order to make what I named a chronology of events based on all of these witness statements, which is, in fact, a criminal analysis and reconstruction of the events day by day based on all these various witness testimonies, including compilation of information of people we did not necessarily interview because they had too little to say; many of them, for example, being in this group of persons who had information about the deportation routes. So spots where they saw dead bodies alongside of the road, a group of prisoners in different locations, these ones initially were not the main focus, except to understand, more or less, the ambiance of what happened in that area that day. The focus was more on people who had crimes to report, and mainly survivors of what was told at that time being mass executions, and who we could not believe until we had found evidence on the ground that could, indeed, confirm that we were not under the influence of any kind of propaganda.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And can we go to 6231A, which is the Dutch version, and the very last page of the Dutch version, which is page 12. And for brevity, I will state that in page 6 of the English version of this, page 7 of the B/C/S version, Mr. Egbers says that there were Bosnian prisoners of war at the soccer field at Nova Kasaba. And can we blow this up a bit. And I don't know if you can read it, but we see a rectangle, and it says above the rectangle: "Muslim people on their knees; civilians in uniform." And then below that it says: "Almost the whole field covered with people." There's no time mentioned, for the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Is this a document you would have relied upon in your investigation in determining the number of people on the soccer field and, for example, the credibility of the witness who has testified here on that very point?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for sure, in terms of credibility that there were prisoners on the soccer field, but again not to make any assessment on the numbers. It's very difficult to assess numbers in such situations, first, because, again, the situation was moving in time, and also because no one had a computer in his head to make a very precise assessment on how many people constitute a gathering. It's a very difficult exercise. But the main point was not to know precisely how many people went through that soccer field, but then what was their fate.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And do you have any reason -- did the investigation have any reason to doubt Mr. Egbers' conclusion in this document that almost the whole field was covered with people?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have no reason to put in doubt this statement of Mr. Egbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And did you review, on the same subject, intercepted conversations that the Bosnian Muslim Army intercepted from the Serb forces, and did you review them with this same issue in mind?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. That reminds me of something. And we also had an information, I think, through that type of source that initially there was the will to bring down from Bijeljina some investigative judge who was supposed to assist in the scanning of these people in order to maybe identify some war criminals among them. I think that was the source, it was from intercepts, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let me show you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, could I please have a reference to the intercepts that Mr. McCloskey is now referring, because we haven't mentioned any intercepts here. We were actually trying to refute some other aspects.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I was first laying the proper and appropriate foundation, that he would have reviewed intercepts on this same topic that was an extreme challenge by General Tolimir, the number of people -- or the people on the football field. There's also a topic that I'm going to, and that is the -- if you recall, the very symmetrical photograph -- aerial image of the symmetrical squares that were the subject of questions -- natural questions -- inappropriate questions by the Judges. And I have perhaps some information that Mr. Ruez may have relied upon and that might refresh his recollection on this very issue as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If we could go to 65 ter 2948. A is the English, and B is the B/C/S. And because of time, I will just briefly summarise as we go, but then I will -- this is an intercept from 13 July 1995, from 1009 hours. According to the intercept operator, it's between a person named Zoka, Zoka P. and Beara. And it starts out with Beara speaking. I won't read it all, but we see some of the things Mr. Beara is saying. As we see: "Do you hear me? Do you know that 400 balijas have shown up in Konjevic Polje?" L says: "I know." It goes on for a while. Beara eventually says: "Shove them all on the playground. Who gives a fuck about them?"

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, this term "playground" in English, how does that -- what does that, in your experience, get referred to sometimes in the Bosnian, if you know?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But now, indeed, I remember this piece of intercept, and the immediate conclusion we -- I mean, I and others who know the area drafted is that the only place could be referring to, when he was speaking about a playground, was this soccer field of Nova Kasaba that is just a few K south of Konjevic Polje. There is no other playground in the area except this soccer field.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And then Beara goes down and says: "Yeah, well, line them up in four to five rows." Do you remember that particular reference now in your investigation?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The instance shot of the aerial imagery that was shown shows, indeed, people lining in a few rows, but again I would have to say something I already said. That photograph was an instant shot. Sometime later, it could have been 10 or 15 rows. God knows.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Now, let's go to another intercept, 65 ter -- actually, I think I'll skip that one, in terms for brevity of time. Let's go to another one, 65 ter 2961A. B is the B/C/S. Mr. Ruez, I want to first ask you, as this comes up, to see if you recall it. And it's from 13 July, at 1730 hours, and it's between X and Y, as we see from the English. And it begins with X saying: "Is it possible for us to send about ten buses from Bijeljina?" Y says: "Well, tell them right away to come. There's about 6.000 of them now." X says: "Of military age?" Y says: "Shut up, don't repeat." X says: "Okay, then I'll send them." Y says: "Yeah, send them. I have three points; fuck it. There's one where you and I were, then there's one up there where the check-point at the intersection is and there's the one halfway between the check-point and the loading place." X says: "So, over there as well?" Y says: "At each point, there are roughly 1.500 to 2.000." Do you recall this intercept?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't recall this one. It is most certainly in the package of the more interesting ones, but, no, I have no recollection of that one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And in your book of what you refer to as "regroupment" sites, sites where large amounts of prisoners were held, how many main sites were there that you talked about in your book?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mainly -- mainly two big ones, the soccer field of Nova Kasaba and the field at Sandici. But nearby Sandici, we know there was also an additional location that was used to keep people until they could be transported to Bratunac. But the two main locations -- also this little hangar at the intersection of Konjevic Polje, but the two big ones were the soccer field and Sandici Meadow.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I want to ask you about the exhibit. It's the 17 July photo of the Branjevo Farm, Exhibit P94. It's page 223 in your book. That's the one that you will recall shows, according to the United States and according to your assessment, bodies lying in the field on the 17th and excavators digging a mass -- digging a mass grave not far away; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And you, in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, please pause for a moment. Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, what Mr. McCloskey is saying now was not in my cross-examination. This is a redirect that has nothing to do with anything. These intercepts were not verified. This had absolutely nothing to do with my cross-examination. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Do you object to the intercept records you saw or do you object to using this photo, this photograph? Mr. McCloskey --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, objection. First of all, I object to this photo being used, and also I object to the intercepts being used, because we haven't really verified whether these intercepts were noted down by hand. We haven't heard witnesses testifying about that. And, secondly, this more --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. I just want to know if you object to using this photo. Mr. McCloskey, the Chamber is heavily concerned to use this, because that was not part of the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: But I think you'll recall it was, Mr. President, if you hear me out. You'll recall a very strong attack by General Tolimir suggesting that there were battle casualties in the mass graves. In fact, I think Judges asked some questions on that point. If you'll recall, Mr. Ruez, in response to that, said that the time-frame involved that this digging and these holes were opened up and then closed would have not allowed for battle casualties to be taken there. That was one of the things he said. And then he said there are engineering records that show the time-frame involved. Now, when an investigator says something like that, he gets challenged by that on a key issue of the case, all I'm asking him is, is it reminding him of the engineering equipment we see? And then the next thing I'm going to go to is the engineering record to see if he remembers that and if that is what he was talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: In that case, it would be very helpful if you could give a reference to the Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, but we're not there yet. We first need to establish that there is excavating -- engineering equipment on 17 July. And that's all I'm using this for, a document that's already in evidence. That's as simple as that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Judge Nyambe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: I think, Mr. McCloskey, just to add on to what the Presiding Judge has said, it would help all of us, since you are in re-examination, when you are examining that particular evidence, to say, for example, At page so-and-so, the witness said this, the cross-examination was like this, and you're examining following, because the impression given now here is that you are probably -- I'm confused, as if you're opening your evidence-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I normally do that. With the time-frame and the need to get this witness back, I thought everyone would remember the challenge suggesting that there were battle casualties in the mass graves, and that's the issue which I'm sure everyone remembers that I am specifically rebutting here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Therefore, it would be helpful if you just put questions to the witness, and you don't need such a picture, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Could we go to -- the transcript reference, Your Honour, is 1543, lines 1 through 23, on this particular issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And if we could go to 65 ter 781.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And as we get -- Mr. Ruez, were any engineering records captured during the investigation, any of VRS engineering records?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were captured when we did the search at the headquarters of the Zvornik Brigade. That was in 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. If we could go to page 2 in the English and page 6 in the B/C/S. And we need to blow up the English to the date 17 July, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And as you're seeing these, do these forms look familiar to you, Mr. Ruez, just generally?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did. They no longer do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. We need to -- sorry. We need to see the date.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No, we need to go the other direction. 17 July: "Base - Standard, Branjevo." "Base - transport of 700 loader."

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That does that mean anything to you, Mr. Ruez?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: M'mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Does it have anything to do with the testimony that you gave in response to this challenge that there may be battle casualties in this Branjevo mass grave?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This confirms that the burial of the bodies of those who were killed the 16, both we know was at the Branjevo Farm, but also the reburial of those at the Pilica Dom to the Branjevo Farm, was, indeed, conducted on 17 July, Standard being, in fact, the location of the Zvornik Brigade in a former factory named Standard, and Branjevo being the Branjevo Farm. And that event happened, according to these archives, the 17 of July, which matches the aerial imagery that we have where the trench in which people were buried is already fully opened the 17, and there is an excavator seen also on this picture. And on the area where we see the bodies on this picture, most of them have already been removed, since we know the size of the initial execution site.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We are running out of time. Mr. Tolimir, you want to raise something? Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, this is a reference to the 17th. That's number 1. Second, I don't have the document in Serbian before me, so I don't know what it states there. Now, what we saw earlier was not on the 17th in Kasaba, so this was not anywhere in the transcript. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The Chamber is in a very unpleasant situation. We were told that the witness is only available today, where there was some time pressures on the accused. Now, on the Prosecution, you have indicated you would need half an hour. You have had half an hour, and the Chamber would like to put some questions to this witness as well. There were some things we want to clarify. What are your proposals? I think it was not a very efficient hearing this afternoon, and even the days before. We were dealing with a movie for a very long time, and this is a heavy concern of the Trial Chamber. I think we have to consider and to think about the conduct of a trial of the parties. How shall we proceed, Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have a minute and a half, no more documents, just one more point in response to this issue, to see if Mr. Ruez can help us with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Okay. Then use these one and a half minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: But then I will, of course, sit down. And in these situations, as you know, the interpreters have -- you know, better than I, they have worked hard, and sometimes they agree to stay late.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] And we all have to apologise. Please put your last question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, I think, and General Tolimir will agree, that Muslim battle casualties in the area south were in this area that you've referred to above the Kravica hills, sometimes referred to Bare, Kamenica, Ravne Bullen [phoen], and in the Baljkovica area, up in the Zvornik area, where the column pushed through, is that correct, towards Nezuk?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Are both those areas laced with mines from both sides, land-mines?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, most of these places are at risk of being mined, indeed, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you find one shred of evidence that the Bosnian Serb Army, in the days of 13, 14, 15, 16 July, when they're having to deal with this column, would have gone into this land-mine area that's full of Muslims and picked up, you know, dead Muslims and hauled them sometimes 20 kilometres away and put them in someplace like Branjevo Farm?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No evidence at all about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I have no further question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: There are very few minutes left. Judge Nyambe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Yes, I just have a few questions for the witness. The first one is: At the time of your interview with "The Monitor," were you still working for the OTP?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We should check the date, but I think I had just left the OTP. I left the OTP April 7, 2001, so I have no precise recollection of the date this article was published. I think I had just left the Tribunal, but I was still in the Netherlands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Can you recall, was it one year later, two years later, three years later.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no, it was -- I would think it was done in April 2001.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: And when you did the interview with the Parliamentary Committee?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was still at the OTP at that time, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: And the third question is: When you were in the investigation team for this case with Mr. McCloskey, what was your position ?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was then an investigation team leader.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: What level?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: I think that's all. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. May I clarify one thing. During the hearing of the 29th of March, that is, page 953, line 15, to page -- to the next page, line 3, you were referring to bodies in a mass grave, and I would like to quote. Your answer was: "Initially, the assumption was that we thought we had to count 50 people by bus, and I think that, indeed, at the end of the exhumation it was more or less precisely that number that was found." Several lines down, you said: "Most --" no, I don't say you said. It is recorded: "Most probably because the number involved was not sufficient to spark a reburial process, 50 victims, unfortunately, in this case is not a large number." First you said "50 people," and then "150 victims." Could you clarify this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because the witness who led us to work on this situation and ultimately find the location of the killing and burial place said that three buses entered the valley, followed by -- escorted and followed by an APC, and sometime later an excavator came. So it's three buses, 150 potential victims. And, indeed, this is the report of Bill Hagland that the general was shown, and it was, indeed, I think, precisely 150.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. That clarifies the situation. And on the 30th of March this year, at transcript page 1050, line 23, you spoke about the Luke school, and you were asked: "We see the yellow mark over the village of -- well, I can make out 'Branjevo.'" And your answer was: "Pilica, Luke School." And then some lines down you spoke about the school of the location named Kula, close to Pilica. Can you clarify this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I might have said something wrong at one point, because Luke is, in fact, the school that was the concentration spot for the prisoners who -- I mean, for those who managed to get on board of buses leaving Potocari, but on the final destination, before arriving at the confrontation line at Kladanj, they were taken out of these buses and put in this small elementary school, which is the Luke School. At Orahovac, now I don't remember, because initially we call it the -- I've forgotten the name. We changed the names of these places at one point to make them more accurate. I don't remember the name of the one connected with Orahovac. Kula is the one that is close to Branjevo Farm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think there are two different locations.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kula and Luke are two very different ones --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Luke is completely at the south-west and Kula is completely at the north.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: One last question by Judge Nyambe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: It, indeed, is going to be one last question. When I asked you earlier on what your position was when you were investigating, you said you were a P4?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Would you know what position Mr. McCloskey was at the time, as senior legal adviser.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was P4 also.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Can you be precise?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was P4 staff also.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: You're sure?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not 100 per cent sure, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just as an officer of the Court, I think that's something I can certainly tell the Court. I was a P4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. At page 41 of today's transcript, line 15, there's a reference to page 9, line 21 to 22 of the transcript. That was the transcript of yesterday, just to clarify the situation. We are more than running out of time, and I have to apologise, on behalf of all present here in the courtroom, but I want to -- especially for the court recorder and the interpreters, but we have to adjourn and resume next week on Thursday. I would like to tell especially the Defence we would appreciate that you take into account the decision of the Chamber of the 24th of February, the order concerning guide-lines on the presentation of evidence, especially the time-limits of 24 or 48 hours before the examination. And that was not appropriate, what happened today and yesterday. That was the first point. The second point is the kind of presentation of the documents should be better prepared. We had several situations today when it was really confusing for the Registry, for the interpreters, and so on. That should be much better prepared. And the Defence, Mr. Tolimir, you should think about relevance of some questions you have put to this witness today. You should think about that, and otherwise you will get some more guidance. Everybody should be aware of the time we have in this trial. And with these remarks, please take them into account for the preparation of the next witnesses. We have to adjourn, again with apologies for all those who helped us, the whole staff of the Tribunal. We adjourn and resume next week, Thursday. And I forgot a very important topic. Mr. Ruez, thank you very much that you came to The Hague again with many difficulties, I know, because of the volcanic eruption, and we have had you for several days now. Thank you very much for your attendance, and you may return to your normal activities. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
